skills.name: exploit-design
skills.description: Turn one confirmed primitive into a demonstrated effect by climbing reproduce, control, escalate, prove — choosing the sink and the observation before writing the payload, and reaching the effect the primitive actually enables.

workflows.description: Climb from a stored reproduction to control of the object the primitive acts on
prerequisites: A confirmed claim whose execution is tested on the recorded revision, a stored payload, and a verified environment.
steps: Replay the stored payload twice on the recorded revision and keep the control run that differs only in the payload.
Shrink the payload one field at a time until removing that field stops the effect; that field is the primitive.
Vary the one input you claim to control and write the two expected outcomes down before sending either.
Re-store the payload and the environment if either changed, so the claim cites the bytes that actually ran.
observe: The response diff between payload and control, together with the target's own log line naming the request
wall: The effect survives the control run only intermittently, which is a reproduction rate, not control.

workflows.description: Take observed control to the boundary crossing and the artifact that proves it from the far side
prerequisites: Observed control of the object the primitive acts on, and the boundary observed as the effect.
steps: Name the boundary and the single operation that crosses it, then check whether that operation needs a second primitive.
Perform the crossing and read the evidence from the far side, not from the payload's own output.
Store the observation with its timestamp and environment fingerprint, and rate the rung that was observed.
observe: A record, file hash, socket or target log line that exists after the step and not after the control
wall: The crossing needs a second primitive, which belongs to a chaining task rather than to this one.

skills.name: web-injection-to-exec
skills.description: Push a confirmed web injection — SQL, shell, template, expression, deserialization, traversal, XXE — past reflection into a file observation and then into execution, with the marker, the context and the negative control that decide each rung.

workflows.description: Move from a reflected marker to an observation the payload cannot fabricate
prerequisites: A confirmed claim showing the value reaches an interpreter, the named engine, and the context the value lands in.
steps: Send a harmless marker and the control without it, and compare the two responses.
Escape the context the value entered and confirm the escaped payload still produces a predictable difference.
Read the effect through a second interface or a callback so the observation does not come from the payload.
observe: The marker appearing without the control, then a file hash, stored row or callback timestamp produced by the target
wall: The sanitiser survives every context escape, which is a wall to report rather than a licence to permute encodings.

workflows.description: Take an established observation to one command the target runs, and read its side effect
prerequisites: An observation that the interpreter acted, plus a write or execution route the target itself reaches.
steps: Pick the shortest route from the observation to execution and perform one step of it.
Run one binary with one argument, avoiding an interactive shell and anything that alters service state.
Read the command's own side effect from the target's log, a created file or an arrived connection.
observe: The executed command's side effect, quoted from the target's own output or filesystem
wall: Write without execute: the upload directory is writable but nothing executes it, so the effect stays file write.

skills.name: ssrf-to-internal
skills.description: Take a server-side fetch from "the target made a request" to "the target read an internal service", mapping the reachable network, the parsers that disagree about the URL, and the metadata endpoints that hold credentials.

workflows.description: Establish which destinations answer through the target when the fetched body never comes back
prerequisites: A confirmed claim that the target performs the fetch, a listener the target can reach, and the internal ranges reachable from it.
steps: Confirm the fetch happened from the target's side by a callback with a source address and timestamp.
Send one destination at a time and record status, length, timing and error text for each.
If a URL check exists, test whether the validator and the fetcher read the same URL the same way.
observe: A callback arrival, or a response difference between an open and a closed destination measured over five runs
wall: No callback and no reflected body leaves the fetch blind, which is a wall for chaining rather than a reachability claim.

workflows.description: Read data that only the internal destination holds, through the fetch the target performs
prerequisites: A destination that answers through the target and a service whose response identifies what it is.
steps: Pick the internal service whose content proves reachability rather than merely answering.
Read the smallest document that identifies the service, and quote its path without any secret value.
Record what was reached, through which input, and what remained refused by a check or absent.
observe: The internal service's own response content, with the destination and the input that reached it
wall: A metadata credential document is a secret: quote the path, never the key material, and do not use it here.

skills.name: binary-exploit-ladder
skills.description: Climb from a reproducible crash to a demonstrated effect on a native binary, with the real mitigation posture of the target build deciding which technique is even open and a crash never counted as proof.

workflows.description: Move from a reproducible crash to an access that follows the bytes you choose
prerequisites: A confirmed memory-safety claim on the named artifact, its hash and build id, and a control input that does not crash.
steps: Read the mitigation posture from the binary and record each flag with the evidence that showed it.
Reproduce the crash twice with the same input and compare the signal, fault address and stack top.
Shrink the input and then vary the controlled bytes until the fault address or a register holds your values.
observe: Two crash signatures that match, then two chosen inputs producing two predicted fault addresses
wall: A crash that does not move under input is control of a fault, not of execution, and the step stops there.

workflows.description: Turn observed control into an effect the application could not otherwise reach
prerequisites: Observed control of an address, register or object, and the privilege boundary it reaches.
steps: Choose the smallest effect the recorded posture permits and preconditions for it from the same table.
Perform the effect and observe it from outside the payload, under the privilege the target runs with.
Record the environment facts that would differ in production, including ASLR and sandbox state.
observe: The target process's own output, a created file or a connected socket after the step
wall: Full RELRO with PIE and no leak closes the overwrite; the next step is a leak primitive, which is another claim.

skills.name: credential-and-pivot
skills.description: Take a credential from "it exists" to "here is every door it opens", verifying it with the smallest act, reading the privilege it carries from the system's own data, and pivoting through each further door that privilege reaches.

workflows.description: Establish that the credential is usable and whose privilege it carries, before using it
prerequisites: A confirmed claim showing a credential is reachable, the principal it belongs to, and the system that accepts it.
steps: Check the material's format, issuer and expiry, and set aside placeholders from templates and examples.
Verify once with the smallest act that answers whether the principal works, and record the identity returned.
Read the privilege map from the system's own authorization data rather than from the credential's name.
observe: The identity the system returned for that credential, with the timestamp of the single verification
wall: A refused verification or a recorded lockout is a result to report, not a dead end.

workflows.description: Walk the privilege map from the first system through every further door it opens
prerequisites: A verified principal and the privilege map read from its system.
steps: Choose the operations that prove access at that privilege, starting with the system that accepts the credential.
Perform each and read its result from the target's own data or log.
Record every door the credential opens as you walk through it, and redact the secret from every artifact.
observe: The target's own record or log line showing the operations performed by that principal
wall: A credential that reaches further than the map suggested is the pivot: each new system it opens is a door to record and walk through.

skills.name: session-to-root
skills.description: Take a demonstrated shell or in-band command execution to a root observation of the compromised workload — enumeration discipline, the path menu from sudo to the container boundary, the receipt that backs a root claim, and the honest wall when the boundary holds.

workflows.description: Establish the foothold's identity from the target side, then walk the privilege menu and record the check closing each path
prerequisites: A confirmed claim whose effect is a command the target ran, with the receipt and the control that did not run it.
A transport that can carry further commands: in-band through the exploited service, or a listener on an operator lab network.
steps: Run one command that reports the foothold's user, groups and host, and record the receipt before attempting anything else.
Walk every path-menu entry once and record, for each, what would be written or executed and the check that would refuse it.
Cross with the smallest reversible operation and read the effect from the system's own answer rather than from the payload.
Corroborate the new identity with a root-only operation observed independently, and clean up everything the attempt created.
observe: The identity receipt from the target side, then a root-only artifact such as a file read or write that the former identity was refused
wall: Every menu entry is closed by a named check, which is the boundary to report rather than a reason to guess.

workflows.description: State which boundary the root observation crossed, corroborate it a second time and leave the target as it was found
prerequisites: A root observation with its identity receipt and one corroborating root-only artifact.
steps: Repeat the observation through a different command or transport so the claim rests on two independent reads.
Name the boundary crossed: the workload's namespace or account, never host kernel and never a container escape.
Remove every process, file, account and service change created, and record each removal with a receipt.
Record the rungs not reached, the check that stopped each, and any change that could not be avoided.
observe: Two observations of the same identity from different commands, and the cleanup receipts
wall: A state change that cannot be reversed makes the step a limitation to report, not a silent cost.

skills.name: internal-pivot
skills.description: Carry a foothold into internal reach — an in-band request the compromised host makes, a reverse shell into the operator's lab listener, a recorded callback — and state the network facts instead of assuming them.

workflows.description: State the network facts, name a destination from the target's own data and make the request in-band
prerequisites: A tested claim for a command or request the target side performed, with its receipt and control.
The foothold's identity and network position recorded: address, resolver, proxy and container context.
steps: Write down sandbox reach, target reach, configured ingress and transport before the first probe.
Choose a destination the target's configuration, resolver or error text names, and quote the source.
Send one in-band request per destination with the same request to a known-closed destination as the control.
Record body, status or timing per destination and keep the sandbox's own requests in a separate column.
observe: A response or timing difference between open and closed destinations that the control does not reproduce
wall: A request that cannot be shaped through the service leaves the destination untested rather than unreachable.

workflows.description: Turn a blind request into an arrival record, or state the ingress fact that made it invisible
prerequisites: A destination named from the target's own data and an ingress path the run actually configured.
steps: Aim the blind request at the recorded lab listener or the operator callback and record the arrival with its source address.
Use a lab-network reverse shell for one command's output only, then close the process that carried it.
Bound the sweep to the destinations the target's own data named, with a control for each open and closed result.
Record every destination touched so the report states the breadth instead of implying it.
observe: The arrival record with source address and timestamp, or the absence plus the egress test that explains it
wall: No lab network means no listener; in-band requests and a recorded callback are the remaining observations.

skills.name: n-day-to-effect
skills.description: Take a patch diff or an advisory lead to a triggered effect — test applicability against the installed artifact, build the trigger from the change, and never count a version match as proof.

workflows.description: Turn an advisory or patch lead into a statement about the installed artifact's code, not its version
prerequisites: A lead with an identity: a changed revision, a patch, an advisory identifier or a regression test.
The installed artifact reachable for inspection: source, shipped file, image digest or a bounded disassembly.
steps: Read the change and name the function, the check and the input that reaches it.
Find that slice in the installed artifact and record whether the correction is present, with the hash or build that anchors it.
Record the claim as an open proof gap until a trigger shows an effect; a version match stays a lead.
observe: A named code slice missing the check, plus the route that reaches it
wall: A stripped or bundled artifact that cannot answer the question is a named missing artifact, not a version verdict.

workflows.description: Build the trigger from the change, observe the effect from the target's side and record the claim honestly
prerequisites: A named vulnerable slice in the installed artifact and a route that reaches it.
steps: Write the predicted difference for the trigger and for the control before sending either.
Shrink the input until removing one more field stops the effect, and store the bytes that ran with their hash.
Observe the effect away from the payload and state the depth: crash, read, write or execution.
Record closure, execution, proof and policy basis from what the trigger established, with same-run receipts.
observe: An effect artifact that moves with the trigger and not with the control, with its depth and timestamp
wall: A trigger that needs a precondition the run cannot build is a needs edge, not a confirmation.
